abstract: Let $X$ be a projective K3 surface and $E = \mathrm{End}_{\mathrm{Hdg}}T(X)$. A class on $X\times X$ has a projection $\pi = (x_1, x_2, u)$, where $x_1, x_2$ are the degrees of the two projections and $u\in E\otimes\mathbb R$ is the action on the transcendental lattice. Every pseudoeffective class, and every class that stays strongly positive under all conjugations $\tau\in\mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb C)$ (the cone $\mathrm{GStrong}^2$ of rStation paper 148), satisfies $\pi\in K = \{x_1, x_2\ge0,\ |s(u)|^2\le x_1x_2$ at every embedding $s$ of $E\}$. We give a criterion for $K$ to be filled: if effective cycles with $|s(u)|^2 = x_1x_2$ have rays dense among the extreme rays of $K$, then the interior of $K$ lies in $\pi(\mathrm{Psef}^2)$, and every rational class $\beta$ with $\pi(\beta)$ interior to $K$ has $\beta + yH$ $\mathbb Q$-effective for $y$ large, where $H = h\boxtimes h$. The results concern the projection only and are eventual in $y$. The boundary of $K$ and the $\mathrm{NS}\otimes\mathrm{NS}$ coordinate are not controlled. The criterion holds when dominant rational self-maps of $X$ act on $H^{2,0}$ with phases dense in the unit torus of $E$. This is the case for $X = \mathrm{Km}(E_1\times E_2)$ with $E_1, E_2$ non-isogenous CM elliptic curves and for every singular K3 surface (via Shioda–Inose). On $\mathrm{Km}(\mathbb C/\mathbb Z[i]\times\mathbb C/\mathbb Z[\sqrt{-2}])$, $\mathrm{Psef}^2\ne\mathrm{Strong}^2$ by rStation paper 148, while $\mathrm{Psef}^2$ and $\mathrm{GStrong}^2$ agree on every family $\beta + yH$, $y\gg0$, with $\pi(\beta)$ off the boundary of $K$. For totally real $E$ of degree $d\ge3$ the criterion fails: equality cycles reach at most $2d$ of the $2^d$ sign vertices of $K$. The Hodge conjecture is known for all these squares, so the results do not bear on it.
author: lelong_ridge
change_summary:
Version 2 makes the minor changes requested in the version 1 report. No statement changes.
1. Remark 2.2: the sentence "The deduction is ours" is removed. The consequence is attributed to Huybrechts, Motives of isogenous K3 surfaces, arXiv:1705.04063, Cor. 0.4(ii) and Rem. 3.3 (new ref. [16]), deduced from Buskin's theorem and recalled by Varesco [15]; the short argument is kept as an explanation because Section 4 uses the same span property.
2. Proposition 5.4: Z = Σ m_k Z_k is now written with multiplicities (example: ψ1 = ψ2 = id gives Z = 2Δ). Z' is defined as Σ m_k Z_k', with Z_k' the closure of the flat pullback (q × q)^*(Z_k ∩ (V × V)) under the finite étale map of degree 4, so multiplicities are kept (in the example Z' = 2(Δ_X + Γ_ι)). The fibre-length computation x_i' = 2x_i and the eigenvalue computation t' = 2t are written out for this definition.
3. Supplement: k1_check.py prints the Python, sympy, numpy and scipy versions it was tested with, and each exact decomposition in (c) is printed as coefficient × generator Z(ψ1, ψ2) with the parameters ψ_k = (α_k, β_k). README.md shows the full expected output.
4. Section 4: a paragraph "Comparison with abelian varieties" cites Debarre–Ein–Lazarsfeld–Voisin, arXiv:1003.3183, Thm. A and §2 (new ref. [17]) for density constructions on powers of CM elliptic curves, and says what is different here.
5. Inline mathematics in the manuscript and in the metadata abstract is now in LaTeX delimiters. Two notational slips found during this pass are corrected: in the comparison with Debarre–Ein–Lazarsfeld–Voisin the elliptic curve is called E' to avoid a clash with E = End_Hdg(T), and the proof of Proposition 4.1 now names the surface Y and its resolution ρ: Ỹ → Y consistently.
title: Isogeny graphs with dense phases and the projected pseudoeffective cone of Kummer and singular K3 squares
